system:
Resolve reference/request licences for each visual attribute. Return only governs and reasons matching the supplied JSON contract. Interpret the complete request semantically, without keyword lists. The separate medium_decision already settles rendering-medium permission and taxonomy: the medium owner is pinned by the schema. Host code computes the style phrase, transformation phrase/target, discrepancy and note from the accepted medium decision. Do not return those host-owned fields.
With no visual reference, every visual attribute is request-governed. Otherwise the reference governs every attribute the user has not actually specified. Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. A stale Asset.Description is caller commentary; actual Card observations govern reference appearance. Independent reference_readings are real supplied readings even when this analysis attaches no conditioning media.
Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. Action authority concerns what the figure is asked to do, not only locomotion; a performance request does not need physical travel. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.
In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed appearance before incoming identity portraits. Incoming replacement/placement images supply identity; their studio lighting/backdrop must not replace the clip's world. For a non-frame content reference, sheet panels, labels, multiple views and posing are presentation, not the new scene or identity. For actual_frame sources, the entire supplied image is the target frame at its anchored instant: preserve those pixels, including their complete layout and source background. Never authorize sheet cleanup on an actual frame merely because it is a sheet. An observed pose is licensed only for an actual frame anchor, never as an identity attribute. Keep rendering restyling independent of retention relationship: changing a medium does not itself select attribute_transfer.
Target identities are already resolved by identity_requirements. Those are TARGET descriptors and properties after explicit caller requirements; original observed_subjects remain the SOURCE. Do not reassert a conflicting source gender/species/age/wardrobe as a request error. Neither re-author those identity decisions nor return identity fields. Resolve only the remaining attribute owners and their reasons.

brief.intent: the woman in the technical jacket rides the dragon into an epic battleground, cinematic hollywood scene with dramatic expressions and camera movements

cards.summary: A vertical eight-panel cinematic character reference sheet for an adult person in black tactical clothing, featuring a rainy rooftop hero shot, front/side/back turnaround views, and close-up detail crops of the face, jacket collar, hands, and boots.

subjects.descriptor: Adult person with a short, dark, side-shaved hairstyle tied into a small topknot, wearing all-black tactical clothing.
attributes: short dark hair with shaved sides and a small tied-back topknot
small visible scar above one eyebrow
black tactical jacket with straps, buckles, and zipper
pose: Top hero panel: standing with feet apart, arms at the sides, and head turned toward frame left
FRONT panel: standing upright facing the camera with arms relaxed at the sides
SIDE PROFILE panel: standing upright in profile facing frame left
BACK panel: standing upright with the back to the camera
FACE panel: close frontal view with a serious, neutral expression
HANDS panel: hands shown close-up with fingers relaxed and slightly curled

subjects.descriptor: Two presentation environments: a rainy nighttime urban rooftop or elevated walkway in the hero panel, and a plain dark charcoal studio backdrop in the turnaround and detail panels.

cards.environment: Top panel: rainy urban rooftop or elevated walkway at night with metal railings, wet reflective ground, and out-of-focus city lights. Lower panels: plain dark charcoal studio background.
cards.lighting: Cinematic low-key lighting; the hero panel uses cool blue-gray night light with warm amber practical lights, while the turnaround and detail panels use soft directional studio light.
cards.framing: Multi-panel vertical contact sheet: a wide full-body hero image at top, a row of three full-body turnaround views, and a row of four close-up detail crops.
cards.style: Photorealistic cinematic character reference sheet or concept-art turnaround with a gritty noir tone.
cards.characterisation: A serious, weathered tactical character presented in an all-black outfit with a gritty, cinematic noir aesthetic.

cards.summary: A dark fantasy dragon character reference sheet featuring a large cinematic hero image above six labeled panels showing front, side, rear, head, wing, claw, and scale details.

subjects.descriptor: Large black-scaled dragon with long pale horns, dorsal spikes, membranous wings, a long tail, and clawed feet.
attributes: crest and row of dorsal spikes
pose: hero image: standing side profile, head lowered toward water, wings partly raised
inset panels: front, side, rear, head close-up, wing membrane close-up, claw close-up, scale close-up

cards.environment: Dark volcanic rocky terrain with glowing orange lava fissures, haze, and shallow reflective water in the hero image; dark neutral backgrounds in the detail panels.
cards.lighting: Low-key, moody cinematic lighting with warm orange lava glow in the hero image and cool soft highlights on the scales in the detail panels.
cards.framing: Composite reference-sheet layout: wide hero scene at top, six detail panels arranged in two rows below.
cards.style: Dark fantasy creature concept art and CGI reference sheet, highly detailed and photorealistic.

rendering_permission.reasoning: The request describes scene action and appends a descriptive style phrase, "cinematic hollywood scene with dramatic expressions and camera movements," but does not expressly authorize transforming or restyling the attached reference’s rendering. The style phrase is metadata-like, not a complete target-rendition directive.

medium_decision.requested_style: cinematic hollywood scene with dramatic expressions and camera movements
medium_decision.reasoning: The rendering permission is host-owned and must be copied exactly: preserve, with empty operation_quote and target. The first observed reference style is a photorealistic cinematic concept-art/character turnaround, which is a digitally drawn illustration under the 2d-animation family; the retained style removes only reference-sheet/turnaround packaging. The request adds action and a cinematic/dramatic filmic phrase but does not name a specific rendering process, so requested_medium remains empty while requested_style keeps the full requested phrase. Treatments are cinematic and dramatic in requested order.
